programme: A SNAI2-centred epithelial-plasticity/TGF-beta module: SOX9's own target list includes SNAI2, and PER2 also targets SNAI2 together with TWIST1 and the TGF-beta output gene SERPINE1 — so SOX9 and PER2 sit as opposing inputs onto the same node. SNAI2 represses the epithelial-adhesion gene CDH1, a target it shares with TFAP2A, which functions here as the epithelial-identity counterweight to Slug-driven plasticity. GSC, an Activin/Nodal-TGF-beta-induced organizer gene (targets BMP4, INHBA, CHRD, FOXH1), supplies a second EMT-type input, and MUC1 is the mucin/epithelial readout that cross-talks with Slug-driven states. Two brakes close the circuit: ZNF165 drives the TGF-beta receptor negative-feedback genes SMAD7, SMURF2 and PMEPA1 (a target TCF7L2 also reaches, alongside SMAD1 and ACVRL1), and ZBTB17 (Miz1) drives the TGF-beta cytostatic arm CDKN2B/CDKN1A/CDKN1C — though ZBTB17 is flagged discordant between the two diseases, meaning this brake is engaged in one direction in one disease and the opposite in the other rather than shared outright. TCF7L2, the Wnt effector of the gut crypt, plugs into the same node set via SNAI2 and PMEPA1.
role_in_a: In IBS the module would run as a barrier/plasticity governor rather than full EMT: PER2 disruption in intestinal epithelium is already tied to barrier dysfunction (PMID 40847793), MUC1 mucin variation is genetically linked to an IBS-adjacent GI disorder (PMID 33608531), and TCF7L2 receptor variants are tied to GI motility phenotypes overlapping IBS (PMID 31691451) — consistent with the SNAI2/CDH1 node modulating mucosal turnover and permeability under stress rather than driving invasion.
role_in_b: In thymoma the same node would run toward tumour-cell plasticity: SOX9 and SNAI2 sit at the top of Open Targets' thymoma percentile ranking (0.948 and 0.885) and MUC1 is also high (0.834), consistent with SOX9 marking thymic epithelial progenitor identity, MUC1 acting as an epithelial/mucin differentiation marker used in thymic epithelial tumours, and SNAI2-driven CDH1 repression underlying the epithelial-to-spindle-cell transition described in more aggressive thymic epithelial tumours.
shared_axis: Both are diseases of an epithelial compartment — colorectal mucosa versus thymic epithelium — that run the same SNAI2/CDH1-centred, TGF-beta-responsive plasticity checkpoint, held in check by ZNF165/ZBTB17-linked negative feedback. The two diseases would share it not because they are linked to each other, but because both tissues reuse the same generic checkpoint under different provocations: barrier stress in the gut, transformation in the thymus.
reasoning: The module is internally coherent from the target lists alone — SOX9, PER2 and TCF7L2 converge on SNAI2, SNAI2 and TFAP2A converge on CDH1, and ZNF165/TCF7L2 converge on PMEPA1 — so it can be named without invoking outside factors. Open Targets independently places SOX9, SNAI2 and MUC1 high in thymoma and MUC1/PER2 in IBS, and three PMIDs place MUC1, PER2 and TCF7L2 in IBS, but nothing retrieved connects IBS to thymoma directly, so the cross-disease link itself rests on the shared-programme reasoning above rather than on a documented association, and ZBTB17's discordant direction weakens rather than strengthens the case that the brake arm is truly shared.
support: PMID 33608531 — GWAS placing MUC1 in an IBS-adjacent GI disorder. PMID 40847793 — disturbed intestinal epithelial Per2 causing a barrier-linked phenotype relevant to IBS. PMID 31691451 — TCF7L2/receptor variant associated with GI motility relevant to IBS. PMID 19513096 and PMID 29245136 are the two 'joint' retrievals (a gonadal-dysgenesis case report and a Drosophila germline stem cell paper) but neither establishes a mechanistic link to either disease and are noted only for completeness.
how_to_falsify: Knock down SNAI2 in parallel in a patient-derived IBS colonic organoid and a thymoma epithelial cell line: the module predicts that high SOX9/low PER2 pushes both toward a SNAI2-high, CDH1-low state (barrier permeability in the organoid, spindle-cell/EMT markers in the tumour line). If SOX9 and PER2 levels do not track with SNAI2/CDH1 output concordantly in both systems, the shared-module claim fails.
caveats: Colorectal mucosa and thymic epithelium have no established comorbidity or developmental lineage in common; the account is built on 40 patient-group comparisons but only one independent cohort pair, so the 'shared module' reading is inferred from a single cohort-pair replication, not many. NFIA, ID2 and GLIS3 were concordant but excluded because their target sets (adipocyte/glial, proliferation/stemness, and pancreatic-developmental genes respectively) do not connect to the SNAI2/TGF-beta node — their absence is not an oversight. Open Targets records no thymoma association at all for six of the nine carrying factors, and ZBTB17 is explicitly discordant between the two diseases, so the cytostatic brake arm should be read as weaker than the EMT-effector arm.
